name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin
description: Czech public register operated by the Ministry of Justice, covering the commercial register, insolvency register and beneficial-owner records.

operator.name: Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR (Ministry of Justice of the Czech Republic)

publicAccess.notes: Record states: free search without registration.

pros: Single portal spanning commercial, insolvency and beneficial-owner registers
Free search without registration
cons: Interface is primarily Czech-language
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04 by fetching or.justice.cz. Operated by Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR.

name: ARES
description: ARES is the Czech Ministry of Finance information system that brings together data on economic subjects held in other registers, including the public register kept by the courts, the trade licensing register and the statistical register. It resolves a Czech entity to its identification number and shows what each source register records, without constituting any of that data itself.

publicAccess.notes: The web application is client-rendered, but its public REST interface returned entity records anonymously without any credential, which is how free account-free access was established rather than inferred from the landing page.

bestFor: Resolving a Czech business name or identification number and seeing at a glance which source registers hold data on it.
A first lookup before going to the register that actually constitutes the fact you need.
notRecommendedFor: Use as the legal source of record, which remains the public register kept by the courts, the trade licensing register or whichever register constitutes the specific fact.
Obtaining a certified extract, which is issued by the constituting register rather than by this system.
recommendedIndustries: Economic subjects recorded in Czech public registers
pros: One lookup reaches data from several Czech registers that are otherwise consulted separately.
The public interface is free and needs no account, and machine access returns structured records.
It is operated by the Ministry of Finance rather than by a commercial aggregator, so the assembly is a government service.
cons: ARES constitutes nothing. Every fact it displays is constituted in another register held by another body, and a legal question belongs to that register rather than to ARES.
Because it assembles data from several sources, a discrepancy is resolved against the originating register, not against this system.
The application renders client-side, so its interactive behaviour, any CAPTCHA and any rate limiting were not observed directly.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official Czech sources. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: NOT ARES. ARES constitutes nothing: each fact it shows is constituted in a different register held by a different body — principally the veřejný rejstřík kept by the registry courts, the živnostenský rejstřík, and the statistical register. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Ministerstvo financí České republiky, which operates ARES as its information system. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately identified from any official page fetched; no external contractor is named, and none is asserted. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The ARES web application at ares.gov.cz together with its public REST interface. Classified corporate-number-database and deliberately NOT company-register or business-entity-register: the type’s own boundary note states that an identifier database is not automatically the legal register of the entity, which is precisely ARES’s position. This is the same distinction the previous wave had to correct for Germany, France and Spain, applied here before publication rather than after.

name: Insolvenční rejstřík
description: Insolvenční rejstřík is the Czech public insolvency register kept under the Insolvency Act, publishing insolvency proceedings, the decisions issued in them and the associated case files. Publication in the register is how insolvency decisions are made publicly effective in the Czech Republic.

publicAccess.notes: The register is served publicly without an account. One legacy entry point returned a server error during verification while the register itself remained reachable, so the working entry point is recorded rather than the failing one.

bestFor: Checking whether a Czech person or company is subject to insolvency proceedings and reading the decisions issued in them.
Following a Czech insolvency case through its published court file.
notRecommendedFor: Confirming that a company exists or who represents it, which is the public register kept by the courts.
Treating an empty result as proof that a party has never been insolvent, because entries are removed after the statutory period.
pros: The register is free to search and needs no account.
Publication in the register is the statutory means by which Czech insolvency decisions take public effect, so the register is part of the procedure rather than a report on it.
The case file associated with a proceeding is published alongside the decisions, so the underlying documents can be read.
cons: It records insolvency proceedings only. It establishes nothing about whether a company exists, who represents it or whether it is otherwise in good standing.
Entries are removed once the statutory retention period expires, so an absent result does not prove that a party was never insolvent.
The register concerns a legal procedure and is not a general assessment of creditworthiness.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official Czech sources, including the register’s own pages citing the Insolvency Act provisions that govern it. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The insolvenční zákon constitutes the register; the insolvency courts enter proceedings and decisions into it, and publication there is what makes those decisions publicly effective. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Ministerstvo spravedlnosti České republiky, which administers the register. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Unknown. The ministry’s own published data-protection notice indicates that processing involves parties beyond the ministry, but no official page fetched names the software supplier, so no technical provider is asserted here. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public ISIR web interface at isir.justice.cz. A legacy redirect endpoint under isir.justice.cz returned HTTP 500 during verification while the register itself was reachable; the working entry point is recorded and the failing one is not published.

name: Evidence skutečných majitelů
description: Evidence skutečných majitelů is the Czech register of beneficial owners, kept under Act No. 37/2021 Coll. and administered by the Ministry of Justice. On 17 December 2025 the Ministry withdrew public access to it, and inspection is now limited to registering persons, public authorities, obliged entities under the anti-money-laundering act and other legally entitled applicants.

publicAccess.notes: Public access was withdrawn on 17 December 2025. The page that previously carried the public search now serves the withdrawal notice instead of a search form, so freeToSearch records the absence of any public search rather than a fee. Access requires authentication — a data box for a registering person’s own extract, or the state identity space or an approved application for remote access — which is why login and identity verification are both recorded as required. No form was reached, so the presence of a CAPTCHA is not asserted.

bestFor: Understanding what the Czech beneficial ownership register holds and on what legal basis, before requesting access through one of the routes that remain open.
Obtaining a legal entity’s own beneficial ownership extract, which the entity can still retrieve by authenticating with its data box.
notRecommendedFor: Public beneficial ownership research. There is no public search at any price since 17 December 2025.
Checking company registration or filed documents, which sit in the public register on a separate system.
recommendedIndustries: Czech legal entities subject to beneficial ownership registration
pros: It is the statutory Czech beneficial ownership register, so an extract from it is the authoritative record of who ultimately owns or controls a registered entity.

The withdrawal of public access, the categories that retain access and the effect on existing remote-access permissions are all stated plainly on the register’s own front page rather than left to be inferred.
Remote access permissions granted before the withdrawal remain valid, and the Ministry opened an automated application route for obliged entities at the same time.
cons: It is no longer open to the public. A member of the public cannot look up any entity’s beneficial owners here.
Every remaining route requires authentication — a data box, the state identity space, or an approved application — so the register cannot be checked anonymously at all.
An entry records who is registered as a beneficial owner. It is not a statement that the registration is complete, current or correct.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the register’s own pages at esm.justice.cz. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register is constituted by zákon č. 37/2021 Sb., o evidenci skutečných majitelů. It is a separate system from the veřejný rejstřík: the register of beneficial owners is expressly not one of the public registers, sits on its own host and rests on its own act. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Ministerstvo spravedlnosti České republiky, which administers the register and which announced and carried out the withdrawal of public access. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not established. No supplier is named on any page fetched, and none is asserted. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The application at esm.justice.cz, which now serves a withdrawal notice in place of a public search and offers authenticated routes instead. Access, established directly rather than inferred: the register’s front page states that on 17 December 2025 the Ministry of Justice withdrew public access to the register, and that it remains accessible to registering persons for their own extract after signing in through the entity’s data box, to privileged users with remote access — public authorities through the state identity space or on application, and entities obliged under the anti-money-laundering act on application — and to other legally entitled subjects on application. Remote access granted before that date remains valid. The page that the register’s own navigation labels as the search in the public part of the register was retrieved and serves the same withdrawal notice rather than a search form, so the absence of any public search was confirmed on the surface that would carry it rather than assumed from the banner. An earlier pass held this record back because the extent of public inspection was unestablished; it is now established, and it is nil. Registry type: beneficial-ownership-register, the only honest type. The record is published rather than dropped because a register that has closed to the public is a fact worth stating plainly, and because a reader who assumes Czech beneficial ownership data is still publicly searchable would otherwise be wrong.

name: ČNB seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů
description: The Czech National Bank publishes a single application over its lists of regulated and registered financial market entities. It offers direct search, the underlying basic lists, and entity counts and time series over the same data.
officialName: Jednotná evidence regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu
nativeName: Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu
englishName: Lists of regulated and registered financial market entities

publicAccess.notes: The application was served directly and anonymously and shows its own menu — direct search, basic lists, entity counts and time series — but no query was executed, so no result behaviour is asserted and no search URL is published. The published address is the bank’s own stable entry point, which redirects to a separate application host where the pages are actually served; the entry point is published rather than the application host because it is the address the bank itself links.

bestFor: Checking whether a financial market entity is regulated or registered in Czechia, and in which population.
Reading the central bank’s own lists rather than a secondary reproduction of them.
notRecommendedFor: Company verification, which is the public register kept by the courts rather than a financial supervisory list.
Treating registration as endorsement. Being regulated or registered is not a statement about solvency or conduct.
recommendedIndustries: Financial market entities regulated or registered in Czechia
pros: It is the central bank’s own application, covering regulated and registered populations together in one system.
Direct search, the underlying lists and statistical views sit in one place, so a user can move between an individual check and the population.
The central bank also publishes web services alongside it, so the same data is reachable programmatically.
cons: It distinguishes regulated from merely registered entities, and the two carry different regulatory weight; a hit alone does not tell a reader which applies.
No query was executed during verification, so result content and any limits are unestablished and none is asserted.
A financial supervisory list does not establish that an entity legally exists, which is a matter for the public register kept by the courts.
The published address is the bank’s own entry point and redirects to a separate application host, so a bookmark or a citation may not land on the address a reader started from.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the application, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The regulatory and registration decisions of the Czech National Bank, taken under Czech financial market law. The application publishes them. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Česká národní banka. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The application is served from the bank’s own host; no external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The unified application reached from the bank’s lists and registers section. Scoping decision: the direct search, the basic lists and the time-series views are one integrated application with one entry point, so they are published as ONE record rather than three. Splitting them would be splitting a system by its own output modes. The bank’s separate central credit register was considered and excluded: it serves credit institutions rather than the public and is not a public register.

name: Seznam advokátů a koncipientů
description: The Czech Bar Association publishes the search over its register of advocates and trainee advocates. Entry in the register is required to practise as an advocate in Czechia, so the search verifies a reserved professional status rather than membership of a voluntary body.
englishName: Search for advocates and trainee advocates

publicAccess.notes: The search was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a person is entered as an advocate in Czechia and may therefore provide legal services as one.
Distinguishing a qualified advocate from a trainee advocate, who appears in the same search but holds a different status.
notRecommendedFor: Assuming every entry carries the same rights. Advocates and trainee advocates are different statuses, and foreign legal service providers appear on different terms.
Treating entry as a statement about the quality of an advocate’s work or the outcome of any matter.
recommendedIndustries: Advocates and trainee advocates in Czechia
pros: Entry is required to practise as an advocate, so the register is a genuine gate rather than a directory of willing participants.
It covers trainee advocates as well as advocates, so a client can tell which status a person actually holds.
It is the chamber’s own search over its own register, which makes it the authoritative Czech source rather than a commercial copy.
cons: It mixes populations with different rights — advocates, trainees, and providers operating under foreign law — so a hit alone does not tell a reader what a person may do.
The chamber notes that services provided under the law of a foreign state are not covered by the collective professional indemnity arrangement, so insurance cover is not uniform across entries.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
An entry records that a person is entered in the register. It does not establish the outcome of any matter, the scope of any indemnity cover, or that an advocate is suitable for a particular case.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the chamber’s own search, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page cites § 24c zákona o advokacii in relation to the collective professional indemnity arrangement, which places the search inside the statutory advocacy framework rather than a membership scheme. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register of advocates kept by the Czech Bar Association under the Czech advocacy act. Entry follows the chamber’s decision and is required to practise. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Česká advokátní komora, a public-law professional chamber rather than a state agency. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: A dedicated search host operated for the chamber; no external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The chamber’s public search over the register. Classification: professional-licence-register, and here the effect genuinely IS a licence to practise rather than a protected title — the contrast with the UK architect and engineer registers in this same wave, which protect titles only. The record states that distinction rather than leaving both to read alike.

name: Seznam notářů
description: The Notarial Chamber of the Czech Republic publishes the list of Czech notaries. A notary holds a state-conferred office rather than an ordinary business licence, and the list identifies who currently holds one.

publicAccess.notes: The list page was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed and no result was retrieved, so nothing about search behaviour or completeness is asserted.

bestFor: Finding a Czech notary and confirming that the person holds a notarial office.
Identifying which notarial office covers a matter, where the chamber publishes office changes alongside the list.
notRecommendedFor: Treating a notary as an ordinary licensed professional. A notarial office is conferred by the state and its number is limited, so this is not a general professional licence list.
Assuming the list explains what any individual notary may do in a particular matter.
pros: It is the chamber’s own list, and the chamber is the body that keeps the record of Czech notaries.
The chamber publishes changes in notarial offices alongside it, so a reader can see that the position is not static.
A notarial office is a state appointment, so appearing on the list carries a stronger meaning than membership of a professional body.
cons: It records who holds a notarial office. It is not a statement about how a notary performs any particular act.
The number of notarial offices is limited by the state, so absence does not mean a person is unqualified — it may mean no office is held.
No search was executed during verification, so search behaviour, coverage and completeness were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the chamber’s own list page, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The Czech notarial code, under which a notary is appointed to an office. The chamber keeps and publishes the list; the appointment itself is a state act. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Notářská komora České republiky, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. No external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The published list on the chamber’s own site. Classification: professional-licence-register. The effect here is neither a pure protected title nor an ordinary licence — it is appointment to a limited state office, and the record says so rather than flattening it into either. Completeness is deliberately not claimed: the list was not exercised and no official statement of completeness was read.

name: Seznam autorizovaných architektů
description: The Czech Chamber of Architects publishes the list of authorised architects. Authorisation is required to carry out selected activities in construction reserved to authorised persons, so it is an authorisation to act rather than only a protected title.

publicAccess.notes: The list page was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so search behaviour, coverage and completeness were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a person holds Czech architectural authorisation and may therefore carry out reserved activities in construction.
Separating an authorised architect from an authorised engineer or technician, who are authorised by a different chamber.
notRecommendedFor: Checking authorised engineers or technicians in construction, who are held by the separate chamber for those professions, not this one.
Treating authorisation as a statement about design quality or suitability for a particular commission.
pros: Authorisation is required for reserved construction activities, so the list verifies an entitlement to act rather than only a title.
It is kept by the chamber that grants the authorisation, which makes it the authoritative Czech source.
It is scoped to architects, which keeps a legally distinct population from being blended with construction engineers.
cons: It covers architects only. Authorised engineers and technicians are in a separate chamber’s list, and absence here says nothing about them.
Authorisation records an entitlement. It is not a statement about the quality of any design or the conduct of any commission.
No search was executed during verification, so search behaviour, coverage and completeness were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the chamber’s own site to its published list, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Czech law on authorised architects and authorised engineers and technicians in construction, under which authorisation is granted and reserved activities are defined. The chamber grants and records the authorisation. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Česká komora architektů, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. No external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The published list on the chamber’s own site. Separation decision: this record and the authorised engineers and technicians list are kept apart deliberately. They are different chambers, different authorisations and different reserved activities, and merging them because both concern construction would misstate what either authorisation permits.

name: Seznam autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků
description: The Czech Chamber of Chartered Engineers and Technicians in Construction publishes selections from its list of authorised engineers and technicians. Authorisation is required to carry out selected activities in construction reserved to authorised persons.
officialName: Výběry ze seznamu autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků
nativeName: Výběry ze seznamu autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků
englishName: Selections from the list of authorised engineers and technicians

operator.name: Česká komora autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků činných ve výstavbě

publicAccess.notes: The page was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. It states that JavaScript must be enabled to use its form, and no query was executed, so search behaviour, coverage and completeness were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a person holds Czech authorisation as an engineer or technician in construction.
Separating an authorised engineer from an authorised architect, who is authorised by a different chamber.
notRecommendedFor: Checking architects, who hold a different authorisation from a separate chamber and do not appear here.
Treating authorisation as a statement about the quality of any engineering work.
recommendedIndustries: Authorised engineers and technicians in Czech construction
pros: Authorisation is required for reserved construction activities, so an entry verifies an entitlement to act.
Engineers and technicians are distinguished within one chamber’s list, which reflects how the authorisations actually differ.
It is kept by the chamber that grants the authorisation, making it the authoritative Czech source.
cons: The page presents selections from the list rather than announcing itself as the complete register, so completeness is not claimed here.
Its form requires JavaScript, so the search could not be exercised and nothing about result content or coverage is asserted.
It covers engineers and technicians in construction only. Architects are elsewhere, and absence here says nothing about them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page titles itself “Výběry ze seznamu autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků” — selections FROM the list — and the record deliberately does not upgrade that into a claim to be the complete register. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Czech law on authorised architects and authorised engineers and technicians in construction. The chamber grants and records the authorisation. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Česká komora autorizovaných inženýrů a techniků činných ve výstavbě, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. No external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The published selections on the chamber’s own site, whose form requires JavaScript. Separation decision: kept distinct from the architects’ chamber list. Two chambers, two authorisations, two sets of reserved activities. Merging them because both concern construction would misstate what either permits, which is why a test pins the separation.

name: Evidence podnikatelů v elektronických komunikacích
description: The Czech register of undertakings in electronic communications, kept by the Czech Telecommunication Office. Entry follows a notification under section 13 of the Electronic Communications Act under the general authorisation regime — it is not a licence — and the register deliberately retains undertakings whose activity has ended.
officialName: Evidence podnikatelů v elektronických komunikacích podle všeobecného oprávnění
englishName: Register of Undertakings in Electronic Communications

publicAccess.notes: Result rows were rendered to an anonymous client with no credential and no payment, and the database reported 2,845 records at the time of verification. Free public reading is therefore observed rather than inferred. Filters offered for business name, company number, municipality, street, network type, service type, certificate number and whether communication activity is currently interrupted or terminated. No filtered query was submitted, so behaviour under a specific search and any rate limit were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether an undertaking has notified the Czech regulator that it provides electronic communications networks or services.
Establishing which networks and services a Czech provider actually notified, down to network technology and service type.
notRecommendedFor: Establishing that a provider is currently trading. The register retains undertakings whose activity has been interrupted or ended.
Checking a messaging or email service. Number-independent interpersonal communications services are excluded from the register.
pros: It records what was actually notified, listing network types from metallic and optical lines to satellite and 2G-to-5G mobile, and service types from fixed and mobile voice to M2M and internet access.
It states its statutory basis directly: notification under section 13 of the Electronic Communications Act.
Results are readable without an account or payment, and the database carries its own update date.
It offers an explicit filter for undertakings that have not interrupted or ended their activity, so a reader can separate current from historical entries.
cons: Entry follows a NOTIFICATION, not a licence. Under the general authorisation regime the regulator grants nothing; the undertaking declares, and the register records that declaration.

The register lists undertakings that "were or are" authorised. An entry alone does not establish that a provider is trading today, which is why the interrupted-or-ended filter exists and why using it matters.

Number-independent interpersonal communications services — email and messenger services — are expressly excluded, so absence does not establish that a communications service is unlawful or unregistered.

Being recorded here proves nothing about spectrum or numbering. Notification as an operator, an individual spectrum authorisation and an allocation of numbers are three separate legal acts kept in three separate systems. A Czech undertaking’s spectrum and numbers are in the regulator’s two other databases.
Records from before 1 January 2022 sit in a separate predecessor database, so a full history may require following the link the regulator provides on each affected entry.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the regulator’s own search-database index, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The database states: "V této vyhledávací databázi jsou uvedeni všichni podnikatelé v elektronických komunikacích, kteří byli či jsou oprávněni k podnikání v elektronických komunikacích (s výjimkou poskytování interpersonálních komunikačních služeb nezávislých na číslech). Databáze obsahuje identifikaci podnikatele a záznamy o veřejných komunikačních sítích a službách elektronických komunikací, jejichž zajišťování a poskytování podnikatel oznámil podle § 13 zákona o elektronických komunikacích." It offers the filter "Vyhledávat pouze mezi subjekty, které v současnosti nemají přerušenou či ukončenou komunikační činnost" and reported "Nalezeno 2845 záznamů" on both passes. Entries predating 1 January 2022 link to the predecessor database "Evidence podnikatelů v elektronických komunikacích do 31. 12. 2021". FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The notification made by the undertaking under section 13 of the Czech Electronic Communications Act, within the general authorisation regime. Nothing is granted; the notification is recorded. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Český telekomunikační úřad, the Czech national regulatory authority for electronic communications and postal services. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the regulator’s own ctu.gov.cz domain, which also serves its numbering, spectrum and postal databases. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search database at ctu.gov.cz. Duplicate decisions: the pre-2022 database is a PREDECESSOR of this one under a superseded classification, not a separate statutory system, and is described here rather than published separately. The regulator publishes fourteen search databases in total; only genuinely distinct statutory systems were published in this wave, and the price barometer and blocked-website list were rejected as candidates because neither records an authorisation.

name: Přidělená čísla a kódy
description: The Czech register of allocated telephone numbers and codes, kept by the Czech Telecommunication Office. Allocation is an individual right granted to an undertaking, which is a different legal act from the notification that puts an undertaking on the operator register, and the database can show the full history of holders of a given number.

publicAccess.notes: The database was served anonymously with no credential, offering search by a whole number, by leading digits, by reference number, by undertaking and by the history of a number, with the full list of undertakings rendered in the selector. Login is therefore recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Finding which undertaking holds an allocation covering a given Czech number range.
Tracing the historical holders of a number allocation over time.
notRecommendedFor: Identifying the retail provider of a specific subscriber line. Allocation is not the same as who serves the end customer, because numbers can be ported.
Inferring anything about spectrum or about a provider’s operator status from a number allocation.
pros: It exposes the history of a number, showing all past holders of the right to use it, which few numbering registers publish.
It can be searched from either direction — from a number to its holder, or from an undertaking to the numbers allocated to it.
It accepts partial numbers, so a reader can work from leading digits rather than needing an exact range.
cons: Allocation is a right of use granted to an undertaking. It does not establish that the undertaking is currently providing service on those numbers.
Because numbers are portable, the holder of an allocation is not necessarily the provider serving a particular subscriber on that number.

Being recorded here proves nothing about spectrum or numbering. Notification as an operator, an individual spectrum authorisation and an allocation of numbers are three separate legal acts kept in three separate systems. This database covers only numbers and codes.
Absence of a number from an allocation does not establish that it is invalid or unassigned; it establishes that it is not covered by an allocation recorded here.
No query was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the regulator’s own search-database index, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The database offers "Hledat celé číslo", "Hledat podle části čísla (dle prvních počátečních čísel)", "Hledat podle čísla jednacího", "Hledat dle podnikatele" and "Hledat historii čísla", the last described as showing "historicky všechny držitele oprávnění k využívání tohoto čísla". The undertaking selector rendered the full list of allocation holders to an anonymous client. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The individual allocation decisions of the Czech Telecommunication Office granting rights to use numbers and codes. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Český telekomunikační úřad. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the regulator’s own ctu.gov.cz domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public numbering database at ctu.gov.cz. Separation decision: kept distinct from the operator register and the spectrum portal on the same host. Three different legal acts — notification, number allocation and individual spectrum authorisation — recorded in three databases by one regulator. All three declare resourceIdentity in the ctu-gov-cz group with distinct systemKeys.

name: Individuální oprávnění a příděly rádiových kmitočtů
description: The Czech database of individual radio spectrum authorisations and assignments, kept by the Czech Telecommunication Office. Unlike the operator register, spectrum is granted individually, and the database covers licensees who are not telecommunications undertakings at all, including amateur, aeronautical and maritime radio.
officialName: Informační portál o údajích udělených individuálních oprávnění a vydaných přídělů
nativeName: Informační portál o údajích udělených individuálních oprávnění a vydaných přídělů
englishName: Portal of Granted Individual Spectrum Authorisations and Assignments

publicAccess.notes: The portal was served anonymously with no credential, offering search by frequency range in kHz, MHz or GHz and separate lists of individual authorisations for the amateur, aeronautical mobile and maritime mobile services. Login is therefore recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content, coverage and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Finding who holds an individual authorisation over a given Czech frequency range.
Checking amateur, aeronautical mobile or maritime mobile radio authorisations from the regulator’s own lists.
notRecommendedFor: Inferring that a spectrum holder is an authorised telecommunications operator. Those are separate legal acts in separate registers.
Treating it as a register of organisations only. It also records individual licensees such as radio amateurs.
pros: It is searchable by frequency range across kHz, MHz and GHz, which is the way a spectrum question is actually asked.
It exposes named service lists — amateur, aeronautical mobile and maritime mobile — rather than requiring a reader to know a frequency first.
It distinguishes individual authorisations from spectrum assignments, which are different instruments under Czech law.
cons: Holding spectrum is not the same as being an authorised telecommunications operator. A spectrum holder may have made no notification under section 13 at all, and an operator may hold no spectrum.
It records authorisations held by individuals as well as by undertakings, so a hit does not establish that the holder is a business.

Being recorded here proves nothing about spectrum or numbering. Notification as an operator, an individual spectrum authorisation and an allocation of numbers are three separate legal acts kept in three separate systems. This portal covers only spectrum.
Absence does not establish that a frequency is unused. Spectrum can be used under a general authorisation in unlicensed bands without any individual authorisation appearing here.
No query was executed during verification, so result content, coverage and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the regulator’s own search-database index, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The portal titles itself "Informační portál o údajích udělených individuálních oprávnění a vydaných přídělů", offers "Vyhledávání podle kmitočtu" with kHz/MHz/GHz units, and lists "Seznamy individuálních oprávnění některých služeb: Amatérská radiokomunikační služba, Letecká pohyblivá služba, Námořní pohyblivá služba". FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Individual authorisations to use radio frequencies and spectrum assignments granted by the Czech Telecommunication Office. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Český telekomunikační úřad. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the regulator’s own ctu.gov.cz domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public spectrum portal at ctu.gov.cz. Duplicate decisions: the regulator’s separate overviews of radio and television transmitters are FILTERED VIEWS of these individual authorisations — the television overview names itself "Přehled platných individuálních oprávnění – televizní vysílače" — and were therefore NOT published as separate broadcast records. The point-to-point fixed-link technical dataset in the 71-76 and 81-86 GHz bands was likewise treated as a technical view rather than a separate statutory register.

name: Evidence provozovatelů poštovních služeb
description: The Czech register of postal service operators, kept by the same regulator that supervises electronic communications. It is included here because the Czech Telecommunication Office officially combines telecommunications and postal supervision, and it records which specific postal services each operator is entitled to provide.
officialName: Evidence provozovatelů poskytujících nebo zajišťujících poštovní služby od 1. 1. 2024
nativeName: Evidence provozovatelů poskytujících nebo zajišťujících poštovní služby

publicAccess.notes: The database was served anonymously with no credential, offering filters for operator, date the business entitlement arose, street, municipality, company number, certificate number, whether to include operators that have ceased activity, and the specific postal services provided. Login is therefore recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a company is entitled to provide postal services in Czechia.
Establishing which specific postal services an operator provides, down to domestic, outbound and inbound categories.
notRecommendedFor: Assuming a postal operator is also an electronic communications undertaking. The two registers are separate and entry in one says nothing about the other.
Assuming every entry is currently trading. The database offers an option to include operators that have ceased activity.
pros: It breaks entitlement down by service category — standard, registered, items for blind persons, printed matter and addressed advertising, each split into domestic, outbound and inbound.
It exposes the date on which the business entitlement arose, so a reader can see how long an operator has held it.
It is kept by the same authority that supervises electronic communications, so postal and telecom supervision are traceable to one regulator.
cons: It is a postal register. It says nothing about whether the operator is an electronic communications undertaking, holds spectrum, or holds numbers.
The database can include operators whose activity has ceased, so a hit alone does not establish that a company is currently providing postal services.
Operators recorded before 1 January 2024 sit in a separate predecessor database, and the regulator provides a link to it rather than merging the two.

Absence does not establish that a company carries nothing. The register records entitlement for the postal services the Act defines, and operators recorded before 1 January 2024 sit in the predecessor database rather than here.
No query was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the regulator’s own search-database index, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The database titles itself "Evidence provozovatelů poskytujících nebo zajišťujících poštovní služby od 1. 1. 2024", offers the filter "Vyhledávat i provozovatele s ukončenou činností" and enumerates the postal services in the categories quoted above. It links to the predecessor database covering the period to 31 December 2023. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The business entitlement to provide or ensure postal services recorded by the Czech Telecommunication Office. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Český telekomunikační úřad, which supervises both electronic communications and postal services. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the regulator’s own ctu.gov.cz domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public postal operator database at ctu.gov.cz. Scope decision: postal is in scope for this wave ONLY because this regulator officially combines telecommunications and postal supervision, which the brief permits. The predecessor database covering the period to 31 December 2023 is a temporal predecessor, not a separate statutory system, and is described here rather than published separately.
